title: Oncologist visit
what: A doctor who checks a suspected tumor, orders tests and treatment, and follows you afterward.
why: If a test found a growth or changes that need checking. Also for follow-up after treatment.
tell_doctor: What bothers you, and since when
What tests have already been done

prepare.title: Documents
prepare.text: Gather all your test results: scans on a disc, reports, and biopsy results.

prepare.title: Questions
prepare.text: Write your questions down in advance. It is easy to forget when nervous.

prepare.title: Support
prepare.text: You can come with someone close to you.

bring: Scans on a disc and their reports
Biopsy results, and slides and tissue blocks if you were given them
Past test results, discharge papers, and reports
A list of your medicines, or the packs themselves
steps: The doctor asks questions and reviews your documents
The relevant area and lymph nodes are examined and felt
The doctor explains what is known now and what needs checking
Tests are ordered, or a treatment plan is discussed
feel: Feeling nervous is normal. Ask about anything that is unclear
after: Have the ordered tests on time
You can take notes or ask for a written summary
Do not start any remedies on your own without your doctor
red_flags: Severe pain, bleeding, or a high fever during treatment: call your doctor or emergency services

faq.q: I was referred to an oncologist. Does it mean I have cancer?
faq.a: No. People are often referred to rule out a tumor. Tests give the answer.

faq.q: Can I bring someone with me?
faq.a: Yes, it helps. They will remember what you might miss.

reminders.text: Oncologist visit tomorrow. Gather all your scans and reports, and write down your questions.
